$comment: The containment rule, as data, read by all three implementations' tests.
A dcs-studio.toml arrives inside a stranger's GitHub release, so every path
it declares gets joined onto a root the user can write to. Three copies of
the rule enforce that: src/core/domain/pathContainment.ts (the extension),
media/manifest-core.js (the webview, which cannot import TypeScript) and
extension cannot reach). They are deliberate copies — the alternative is a
runtime dependency between the sim and the editor — but a rule enforced in
three places is only as strong as its weakest copy.
Two of the three were already held to each other. The Rust one was held to
a hand-retyped table, so a case added here and not retyped there left the
bridge's guard quietly weaker than the extension's. This file is the table
all three read, so adding a case is enough to hold all three to it.
Add a case here first, then watch all three suites fail.

accept.why: a leading `.` segment is a no-op, not an escape

reject.why: drive prefix. The case a component-based guard gets wrong off-Windows: Node's path and Rust's Path both parse this as one ordinary component on Linux and would accept it
drive-relative — resolves against that drive's cwd
NTFS alternate data stream: hidden content beside a file
empty is not a path under anything
names the root itself, not a destination under it
doubled separator — refused rather than silently collapsed
trailing separator, for the same reason
